newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS - EOE interest sparked in Royal Dutch.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - EOE interest sparked in Royal Dutch.

text.p: The sharp fall in the underlying Dutch share market promted quick demand on the European Options Exchange (EOE) on Tuesday with puts on the index itelf and Royal Dutch calls attracting heavy trade.

Dealers said the fact that puts outweighed calls on the index by around 11,800 to 7,800 by late afternoon showed investors had adopted a more bearish view of the market and were taking protection as a result. The number of trades on the index made up more than 30 percent of total business on the exchange.
The U.S. missile strike on Iraq, one factor behind the share price fall, also caused increased interest in all oil stocks.

Royal Dutch was the only the stock in AEX to remain in positive territory during the morning and option dealers said it also attracted a lot of EOC interest on the call side. By late afternoon, there were more than 3,000 calls traded to 630 puts as investors attmpted to cash in on further upside progress.
Elsewhere calls in financials ING and ABN AMRO were also in demand, both banks each trapping over seven percent of trade.
